points.title: Our vision
points.body: A trusted, configurable business operations superapp that helps cross-border programs move from onboarding to qualified introductions, meetings, agreements and ongoing collaboration—without creating a different application for every market or program.

points.title: Our mission
points.body: Give program operators and participating companies one multilingual, white-label workspace that replaces fragmented profiles, spreadsheets, shortlists and post-event follow-up with an accountable operating record.

points.title: Human-governed by design
points.body: Automation may assist with matching and workflow, but sensitive business, compliance, legal, credit and provider decisions remain reviewable, recoverable and auditable.

points.title: Clear, protected scope
points.body: Identity, organization and company access remain explicit. Each organization sees only the data and workflows its role and program permit.

points.title: Starting in Asia, designed to extend

faq.question: Who is Plexus designed for?
faq.answer: Plexus is designed for chambers, trade bodies, associations and event organizers that run cross-border business programs, and for the participating companies they invite or approve.

faq.question: Is Plexus available to use today?
faq.answer: Plexus is in pre-launch. Selected workflows are being prepared and validated with approved pilot programs. Contact the team to confirm what is available for your program.

faq.question: What can a program operator manage?
faq.answer: Depending on the approved scope, an operator can organize company intake, structured profiles, reviewed introductions, mutual acceptance, meetings, agreements, event information, resources and accountable follow-up.

faq.question: How does business matching work?
faq.answer: Structured profile information may help identify relevant connections. The program operator reviews context before sharing an opportunity, and both businesses choose whether it should move forward.

faq.question: Can a business join without a program operator?
faq.answer: Participation is normally connected to an approved organization or program. A business can contact Plexus to discuss the relevant program or ask about a pre-event service.

faq.question: Which languages are supported?
faq.answer: This public website supports English, Bahasa Malaysia and Simplified Chinese. Protected workspaces can support additional configured product languages; each organization's language scope is confirmed during onboarding.

faq.question: How is pricing determined?
faq.answer: Pre-launch pricing is by consultation. Scope depends on the program, participant volume, enabled modules, language requirements and the level of onboarding or operational support.

faq.question: How are decisions and data handled?
faq.answer: Matching, compliance, legal, credit and provider decisions remain human-governed. Access is scoped by role, organization and company, with only explicitly shared workflow records available to participating companies.

faq.question: What happens after a meeting?
faq.answer: Where enabled, the workflow can record outcomes, agreement progress, ownership and the next responsible action so follow-up does not disappear after the event.

faq.question: How do I start?
faq.answer: Choose Discuss your program for a program-operator inquiry. For a specific upcoming visit, use the pre-event service to describe your objectives, target connections and practical support needs.

investmentPage.title: Attract the right investment — not just the most attention.
investmentPage.body: Plexus gives investment-promotion teams, zones and corridor programs a structured way to present projects, qualify serious inbound interest, and coordinate delegation visits that actually land on the ground.

sections.title: Present the opportunity
sections.body: Turn zones, projects and incentives into structured, comparable profiles instead of PDFs and slide decks. Capture sector focus, project stage, land/facility readiness, incentive context and the responsible authority.

sections.title: Qualify serious interest
sections.body: Inbound interest is reviewed for fit and relevance before it reaches your team, so you spend time on qualified investors — not cold noise. Organizer review and mutual acceptance stay in the workflow.

sections.title: Coordinate the visit
sections.body: Move a qualified investor from interest to an on-ground visit: delegation itineraries, site visits, interpreter and liaison support, and a coordinated arrival plan — all in one record.

sections.title: Track to outcome
sections.body: Keep letters of intent and MOU state, named owners and next actions visible after the roadshow ends, so momentum doesn't disappear when everyone flies home.

investmentPage.trustLine: Introductions, incentives and local services depend on fit, availability and the responsible authority. Business and investment outcomes are not guaranteed.

governmentPage.title: Run official delegations with a record you can stand behind.
governmentPage.body: Plexus is a governed operating layer for trade authorities, bilateral councils and economic-development agencies — structured delegations, reviewed introductions, coordinated events, and an auditable trail from first meeting to signed MOU.
governmentPage.primaryCta: Brief us on your bilateral program

sections.title: Delegation management
sections.body: Build the delegation roster with explicit roles, tenant scope and company records, so every participant and organizer sees exactly what they should — and nothing they shouldn't.

sections.title: Governed introductions
sections.body: Official introductions move only through organizer review and mutual acceptance. Matching assists the decision; it never makes it.

sections.title: Bilateral event operations
sections.body: Forums, site visits, interpreter scheduling and liaison support are coordinated in one plan, on-ground and online, writing back to the same record.

sections.title: Agreement & MOU state
sections.body: Signing progress, signatories and agreement state stay visible across both sides of a bilateral program.

sections.title: Governance, audit & reporting
sections.body: Provisioning, privileged-event audit and post-program reporting are part of the platform. Data-residency and provider scope are handled per program — see the capability map for current readiness.

governmentPage.trustLine: Compliance and data-residency scope is confirmed per program with the responsible authority. Some governance and provider capabilities are adapter- or roadmap-stage — see the capability map.
